page: Microsoft Azure D248lds_v7 is a Dldsv7-family virtual machine configured with 248 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel processor. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 496.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes 15,118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff between compute density and memory capacity. With only 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance is classified as a low-memory configuration. This design optimizes qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require massive parallel processing power and high-speed local storage without the overhead of a large memory footprint. The inclusion of over 15 TB of local NVMe SSD storage provides high-capacity, low-latency local data access directly on the host.

This server configuration is designed for compute-heavy and storage-intensive workloads. Appropriate use cases include large-scale batch processing, distributed data processing, local database hosting, and applications requiring high-throughput parallel execution alongside substantial local scratch space.
